record.field: How to filter records: domains are lists of [field, operator, value] triples

## Domains A domain is a **list of [field, operator, value] triples**, one list per condition:
``` [["name", "ilike", "Acme"]] [["move_type", "=", "out_invoice"], ["payment_state", "!=", "paid"]] ```
Never a flat triple, never a dict, never a bare string. Operators: `=`, `!=`, `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`, `like`, `ilike`, `in`, `not in`.
Prefix operators combine triples: `"&"` (and, the default), `"|"` (or), `"!"` (not). Each prefix consumes the two (or one) conditions that follow it.
## Traps - A many2one filters by **id**, never by name. Search the record first, then use the id you found. - `ilike` is the case-insensitive contains every name search wants; `=` on a name misses on case. - An empty domain `[]` means *everything* — never pass one by accident when you meant "no filter yet".
Where products live: product.template holds the catalogue, variants are automatic

## The catalogue New products are ALWAYS `product.template` records. The variants (`product.product`) are created automatically by Odoo - never queue a `product.product` without its template id.
Key fields on the template: `name` (the one field a request always has), `list_price`, `standard_price` (cost), `default_code` (internal reference), `categ_id` (product category), `uom_id` (unit of measure), `type` ("consu", "service" or "product").
## What Odoo fills in Price, currency, category, unit and type all have defaults. A new product with only a name is a complete, valid product - the rest is Odoo's business unless the user or a fetched page says otherwise.
## Lookup by name, act by id Search with `name ilike`, then use the template id you found. A name match is a duplicate to reuse, not a second record to create.
Customer vs vendor bills: move types, payment states and residuals

## Bills live on account.move Both kinds of bill are `account.move` rows; the type tells them apart: - Customer invoices are `move_type = "out_invoice"`. - Vendor bills are `move_type = "in_invoice"`.
Always filter the type. An unfiltered search returns both, and the answer is wrong.
## Payment state is the truth `payment_state` is `not_paid`, `partial` or `paid`. A date in the past alone does not mean overdue - the invoice must be unpaid or partially paid AND past due.
## Money - `amount_residual` is what is still owed. `amount_total` is not. Reporting the total as the debt is wrong. - `amount_untaxed`, `amount_tax`, `amount_total` describe the bill; `amount_residual_signed` carries the sign.
Partners and customers: customer_rank marks a customer, there is no customer flag

## Customers are partners with history `res.partner` has NO `customer` flag. A partner is a customer when `customer_rank > 0` - it has bought before - and a vendor when `supplier_rank > 0`.
## Lookup Search by `name ilike`. A partner's `email`, `phone`, `street`, `city` and `country_id` are the fields worth reading back; the rest is rarely what was asked.
Units live on uom.uom inside categories; there is no product.uom model

## Units The model is `uom.uom`, grouped by `uom.category`. A product's unit is `uom_id`, a many2one to `uom.uom`.
There is NO `product.uom` model. Asking for it fails, and the failure looks like a missing model rather than a wrong name - check the name before assuming the model is gone.
## Defaults Units, dozens and common weights/lengths ship with the database. Pick from what exists; creating a unit is rare and almost never what a question is really about.
Sale order states and invoicing: draft, sent, sale, done and how to invoice

## Lifecycle A `sale.order` moves draft -> sent -> sale (confirmed) -> done. `state = "draft"` means editable; confirmed orders grow delivery orders and invoices, they are not edited in place.
## Invoicing one Do not invoice line by line. `invoice_order` on the order id handles the grouping (down payments, delivery quantities, already-invoiced lines) and queues one card. Report the invoice number and its total from the card - never state a total a tool did not return.
## Lines `order.order_line` holds the lines: product, quantity, price, and the delivered quantity. Delivered vs ordered is the first thing to check before promising anything about stock.
Stock levels live on quants per location; pickings move goods, moves explain

## On hand `stock.quant` rows say how much of a product sits in a location: `quantity` on hand, `reserved_quantity` promised to pickings. Negative or zero quants with open demand is a stockout, not a missing product.
## Movement `stock.picking` moves goods between locations; `stock.move` lines explain each transfer. A delivery that never happened is a picking in an unfinished state, not an empty shelf.
Who may see or change what: privileges, model access and per-record checks

## Odoo 20 has no ir.rule and no ir.model.access Access is privileges (`res.groups.privilege`) plus `ir.access` rows: per model, per operation, per group, with an optional domain. A row with no group is a global restriction and binds everyone, including administrators.
## The agent mirrors the user Every read and every write runs with the asking user's own rights. An AccessError names a real boundary - do not route around it, say it plainly and stop that line of work.
## Check before you queue `diagnose_access` answers whether the user may touch a model or a record, which rows apply, and which fields are group-gated - before a card is queued for a write that would fail at Approve. A refused model means the turn ends with an explanation, not another search.
Field types and how to use them: many2one by id, selections by key, readonly

## Reading - A `many2one` shows as a name but filters and writes by **id**. Search the record first, then use the id you found. - A `selection` stores a key ("consu") and shows a label ("Consumable"). Report the label, write the key. - `monetary` carries the company's currency; `float` and `integer` are plain numbers. `date` has no time, `datetime` has one.
## Writing - `readonly` and group-gated fields refuse at write time. Check with `fields_get` or `diagnose_access` before queuing, not after the approval fails. - `one2many` and `many2many` are never written directly by a simple write; they need their own commands, so leave them out of a `set_fields` call.
Which model holds what: partners, products, orders, invoices, stock, time

## Where things live - People and companies: `res.partner`. Users are `res.users`. - Catalogue: `product.template` (variants auto-create). - Selling: `sale.order` + `sale.order.line`. - Money in/out: `account.move` (`out_invoice` / `in_invoice`). - Stock on hand: `stock.quant`; moving goods: `stock.picking`. - Work: `project.task`; hours: `account.analytic.line`. - People directory: `hr.employee`; leave: `hr.leave`.
This index names the model so a search can start. For field names and relations, read the model itself - never guess a field.
Worked hours live on analytic lines against tasks; a day is 8 hours

## Hours Hours worked are `account.analytic.line` records tied to a `project.task` (and through it, a project). A timesheet entry needs a task, hours, and a date.
## Conventions A day is 8h, a morning about 4h. Hours are a number between 0 and 24 - "all day" is 8, never 24. One card per entry, not one per hour. "today" and "yesterday" are accepted words; anything vaguer needs asking.
How a change lands: one card per write, preview first, multi-field in one go

## One card per change Nothing lands in the database without the user approving a card. A turn that describes a change instead of queuing one has done nothing - the card IS the work.
## The right tool for the write - One simple field: `set_field`. - Several fields on one record: `set_fields`, one card, one approval, one undo. Chaining single-field writes risks a record that is half-updated if the user approves only some cards. - A new record: `create_draft` with only the fields stated or found. - Unsure it will apply: `validate_write` first - a dry run that reports unknown fields, missing required fields and current values, and writes nothing.
## After the queue Say what was queued and what it will do when approved. Never claim a write happened before its card is approved - the card is a proposal, not a result.
